$comment: Permissions for the unattended pestidev cloud routines.
TWO routines now share this repo and this settings file:
- 'Daily job-board scrape (pestidev)'  -> reads prompt.md      (original, live)
- the v2 routine                       -> reads prompt-v2.md   (subagent design)
Both are covered by the allow list below. Task is what the v2 routine needs to spawn the
subagents in .claude/agents/. Task is additive and does not alter the original
routine's behaviour: prompt.md never mentions the agents, and each agent's own
description is prefixed [prompt-v2.md ONLY] so a prompt.md-driven run does not
pick one up opportunistically.
=== MCP transport, added 2026-08-24; made the ONLY transport, 2026-09-15 ===
Andrssss/MyWebsite exposes the registry over MCP:
netlify/functions/ai-mcp.mjs            -> MCP (Streamable HTTP, JSON-RPC) transport
netlify/functions/ai-registry.mjs       -> the original REST transport (still exists site-side,
no longer called by either prompt in this repo)
netlify/functions/_ai_registry_core.mjs -> the one shared implementation both call into
Both prompts now use ONLY the MCP transport for the two registry calls (get_registry,
submit_findings) and for check_titles. There is no curl/REST fallback left in either prompt, and
neither prompt ever handles AI_INGEST_TOKEN: with a tool call, the run never sees the credential
at all, the connector holds it and attaches it to the request. If the connector is not
registered on a given environment, both prompts now say to STOP and report that plainly rather
than fall back to a curl call - there is no working fallback path any more. Removed 2026-09-15
specifically because the REST path required pasting the token out of the routine's stored prompt
into a shell command on every single run, which had repeatedly been this routine's most fragile
step (see the dated incidents below, kept as history for why MCP-only was worth the loss of a
fallback, not as instructions any run should still follow).
The server is declared in .mcp.json at the repo root (name: 'pestidev'), so it travels with a
fresh routine checkout. Its token is AI_MCP_TOKEN, deliberately SEPARATE from the retired
AI_INGEST_TOKEN - rotating one never required touching the other, back when both existed.
.mcp.json references it by env-var name only, so the routine environment must have that variable
set; no token is committed here.
enabledMcpjsonServers names 'pestidev' and nothing else. The routine does not strictly need it
- a cloud session loads project-scoped .mcp.json servers without the interactive 'trust this
project MCP server?' prompt, which only exists in terminal sessions - but it is what keeps a
local interactive run consistent with the routine, and it scopes trust to this one server.
Deliberately NOT set: enableAllProjectMcpServers. It approves EVERY server in .mcp.json without
a prompt and overrides the per-server list above, which makes it strictly broader for no gain
here. This repo is public: with a blanket approval committed, a second entry appearing in
.mcp.json - a merged PR, a careless edit - would be auto-connected and its tools exposed to an
unattended run. With only enabledMcpjsonServers, a new entry stays unapproved.
The three mcp__pestidev__* allow rules are exact tool names, not prefixes - MCP permission rules
match the whole tool name, unlike the Bash prefix matching discussed below. A bare
'mcp__pestidev' would allow the entire server; the tools are listed individually so a
fourth tool added server-side does not silently become pre-approved here.
=== check_titles, added 2026-09-08 ===
A third registry-adjacent tool, read-only: given a batch of listing titles it returns whether
each would pass the API's own IT-relevance/senior-title gates and whether it is a cross-source
duplicate - the same isItJob/isSeniorLike/findCrossSourceDuplicates gates submit_findings applies
at insert time, exposed so a title that would bounce later can be dropped BEFORE a detail-page
fetch. Unlike get_registry/submit_findings, this one is also in site-processor.md's own tools:
frontmatter (see its Step B.5) - safe to extend past the orchestrator because it costs no upload
budget and cannot submit or write anything, and because the isolation boundary here has always
been the per-agent tools: allowlist, not a separate credential per tool (get_registry and
submit_findings already share one AI_MCP_TOKEN). This allow list still has to name it explicitly
for ANY caller, orchestrator or subagent, to reach it at all.
=== get_ats_discovery / submit_ats_tenants, added 2026-09-22 ===
A separate discovery channel, unrelated to job postings: finds NEW company ATS boards (Ashby/
Greenhouse/Lever/SmartRecruiters/Recruitee/Personio/BambooHR/Teamtailor/Workday) that the site's
own daily ats-crawl worker doesn't know about yet, via rotating WebSearch queries the server
hands back (get_ats_discovery), submitted the same way as company-discovery's own candidates
(submit_ats_tenants). This is the ORCHESTRATOR's own call, not a subagent's - it already has
WebSearch in this same allow list, so no new subagent was needed. Costs no upload budget, same
as company-discovery/site-change-check. Built site-side 2026-08-26 (Andrssss/MyWebsite
ats-tenants.mjs, REST) but never actually reachable from this routine until now: the original
plan was a curl+AI_INGEST_TOKEN promptSnippet, which is exactly the shape the MCP-only change
above exists to avoid (a model-composed Bash command with `Authorization: Bearer <token>` aimed
at an external host gets blocked by the auto-mode permission classifier in an unattended run,
same as the old registry REST fallback). So this pair was wired up as MCP tools instead,
sharing the same AI_MCP_TOKEN/connector as get_registry/submit_findings/check_titles - no new
credential, no new connector entry.
=== get_event_sources / add_event_sources, added 2026-09-28 ===
Used by a THIRD routine, 'Event source discovery (Hungarian IT events)', which has no repo of its
own and checks out this one purely to get the 'pestidev' .mcp.json entry + this allow list. Its
prompt is stored inline in the routine (not in this repo) and never reads prompt.md/prompt-v2.md.
The tools read and insert-only extend MyWebsite's event_sources registry (Andrssss/MyWebsite
_event_sources_core.mjs, served by the same ai-mcp.mjs / AI_MCP_TOKEN). Same reason as above: the
routine's old curl+AI_INGEST_TOKEN call to event-sources.js was refused by the auto-mode classifier
(2026-09-28). The job-scrape prompts never mention these two tools.
=== Bash(export:*), removed 2026-09-15 ===
Added 2026-08-24 to cover 'export AI_INGEST_TOKEN=... && curl ...', the compound command the
REST fallback needed (Bash rules match on literal command PREFIX, and that call started with
'export', not 'curl' - see the Bash(timeout:*) note below for the same mechanic). Now that both
prompts are MCP-only and neither ever composes an export command, nothing in this repo issues
'export' any more, so the rule was removed rather than left allowing a shell primitive with no
remaining caller.
Why Bash(curl:*) is broad rather than pinned to bakan7.netlify.app:
Subagents (and, on prompt.md, the orchestrator itself) still fetch company career pages with curl
per the TIME RULE (an outer `timeout` wrapping curl's own limits, always capturing the exit
code) - that traffic is unauthenticated, hits arbitrary company domains, and is unaffected by the
MCP-only change above. Bash rules match on literal command PREFIX, and prompt.md's own examples
vary the invocation; a pinned prefix would deny a legitimate fetch mid-run, and there are many
target hosts, not one. In practice this rule has never actually matched anything either, for the
same reason Bash(export:*) didn't: every real call in both prompts is prefixed 'timeout N curl',
never bare 'curl' - see the Bash(timeout:*) note below. It stays allowed anyway as defense in
depth for the (currently unused) bare form.
Why Bash(timeout:*) was added 2026-08-24, and is still needed:
Bash(curl:*) had never actually matched anything. Rules match on literal command PREFIX, and no
call in either prompt starts with curl - every page fetch is prefixed 'timeout N curl' (and, back
when the REST fallback existed, so were the two API calls). So every GET, POST and page fetch
this repo has ever made fell through to the auto-mode classifier, a non-deterministic judgement
on the whole command text, unless this rule covers it. Confirmed 2026-08-23 by diffing run logs:
the one-line 'export ... && timeout 40 curl ...' form was allowed (HTTP 200, 8 rows ingested),
while the same call split across three lines with an improvised 'cd /home/user/pestidev' was
blocked twice, each time producing zero output. That underlying lesson - one exact canonical
command, no cd, no extra statements - is why page fetches still matter for this rule even though
the API calls that originally motivated it are gone.
Known tradeoff, raised and accepted by the owner: Bash(timeout:*) permits
'timeout <n> <anything>', which is broader than Bash(curl:*) and plausibly reaches past
the git denies below, since 'timeout 5 git push' does not start with 'git push'. The
narrow alternative was pinning specific timeout values, but that re-breaks the moment a
subagent improvises a different timeout value, which is the exact class of failure this rule
exists to stop.
git push/commit are denied: both designs have NO git output - the registry submission is the
only output. The superseded registry-file design pushed to main and failed silently on
every run from 2026-07-17 onward, so not one finding ever reached the DB.
